# Spec & Plan Quality Checklist: Event-Driven Triggers — Asset Dependency Graph

**Purpose**: Validate that the feature's spec and plan are complete, consistent, unambiguous, and testable before proceeding to `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-09-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete. This command MUST NOT pre-check any item.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are requirements defined for what a downstream fired only by `on_missing` (no upstream event) receives, i.e. whether `AGENTBOX_UPSTREAM_<KEY>` vars are present for its declared upstreams? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the content of the handoff file's "report metadata" field defined (which report fields are included), rather than only referenced? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are the valid ranges/bounds for `max_runs_per_hour` and `max_chain_depth` specified (minimum, maximum, zero, negative, non-integer)? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is behavior specified when the `governors:` block in `settings.yaml` is absent, partial, or malformed (fallback to defaults vs. error)? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-014, data-model §Run governor]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for whether a downstream fires once or per-upstream when several declared upstreams materialize for the same matching partition? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are requirements defined for the outcome (single run vs. two runs) when both `on_upstream` and `on_missing` would fire for the same partition? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is behavior defined for a `produces.depends_on` declared on a non-asset (job-only) agent — rejected, ignored, or a no-op? [Completeness, Gap, data-model §Agent definition]

## Requirement Clarity & Unambiguity

- [ ] CHK008 - Is "latest materialization for the matching partition" defined by an unambiguous ordering key (event timestamp vs. run start)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "passes its blocking checks" precise enough to distinguish a materialization that has only non-blocking check failures from one that is fully clean? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the `<KEY>` upper-snake transform fully specified for every allowed asset-key character (digits, multiple `/` and `-`, leading/trailing separators)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, data-model §handoff]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the reference instant for the rolling 60-minute window defined (evaluated at the launch-decision moment)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the classification of every launch path into "automated" vs "manual" unambiguous (schedule, sensor, manual UI, Dagster-initiated backfill)? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is "sane upper bounds" for the governor values quantified rather than left as a subjective term? [Ambiguity, data-model §Run governor]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 - Is the cycle/dangling-reference outcome consistent between the spec ("reload fails … names the assets", §FR-003/US4) and the plan ("skip offending assets, unrelated agents still load")? [Conflict, Spec §FR-002/§FR-003, plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the `chain_depth` for a run fired by a manual upstream stated consistently (spec "root … depth 1" vs. data-model "manual upstream contribution 0")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, data-model §Chain depth]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are the governor defaults (`max_runs_per_hour: 12`, `max_chain_depth: 5`) stated identically across spec, plan, and data-model? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014/§FR-016]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are `on_upstream` and `on_missing` consistently described as "start paused" behind the single `autocond_<name>` sensor everywhere they appear? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005/§FR-009/§FR-010]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is the partition-mapping rule (identity daily→daily) stated consistently between the spec (FR-007) and the plan's constraints, including the same out-of-scope boundary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, plan §Constraints]

## Acceptance Criteria & Testability

- [ ] CHK019 - Can "the refusal is visible in the daemon log" be objectively verified via a defined log marker or message content? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK020 - Is "read-only to the container (a container cannot modify it)" expressed as an objectively verifiable outcome (e.g., an attempted write fails)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK021 - Does each success criterion SC-001..SC-006 map to an observable outcome that a reviewer can check without inspecting implementation? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are acceptance criteria defined for the partitioned-`on_upstream` fallback so a reviewer can confirm the restriction actually took effect (log message + README statement)? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §Assumptions, plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK023 - Does every functional requirement FR-001..FR-021 have at least one acceptance scenario or success criterion tracing to it? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are FR-019 (Depends-on form card), FR-020 (Automation view triggers), and FR-021 (README) covered by an acceptance criterion or success measure, or only asserted? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §FR-019/§FR-020/§FR-021]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 - Are recovery-flow requirements defined for after a governor refusal — is the refused partition retried on a later evaluation or permanently skipped for that window? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK026 - Are requirements defined for concurrent/duplicate triggering of the same downstream partition (idempotency / de-duplication)? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK027 - Are requirements defined for the alternate flow where a downstream has multiple upstreams and only some have a matching-partition materialization at fire time? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012a]
- [ ] CHK028 - Is the primary flow's precondition that "new triggers start paused" reflected as its own acceptance scenario (nothing fires until enabled)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, US1 scenario 4]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK029 - Is behavior specified for a `depends_on` entry naming the asset's own key (a length-1 self cycle), distinct from a transitive cycle? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK030 - Is the distinction between an upstream with an empty output set (`output_files: []`) and a "no materialization" file defined for the handoff record? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012a, data-model §handoff]
- [ ] CHK031 - Is behavior defined when the per-run handoff directory cannot be created or mounted read-only at launch (failure handling)? [Edge Case, Gap, plan §Storage]
- [ ] CHK032 - Are the boundary cases for `max_chain_depth` unambiguous — is the run *at* the limit allowed and only the run *exceeding* it refused? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-016/§SC-005]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK033 - Are latency/timeliness expectations for detecting an upstream materialization and firing the downstream specified (e.g., sensor evaluation cadence)? [NFR, Gap, Spec §User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK034 - Are the handoff mount's isolation/security requirements (read-only, no added network reach or credentials) stated as verifiable requirements consistent with Constitution I & V? [NFR, Consistency, plan §Constitution Check]

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Ambiguities

- [ ] CHK035 - Are the assumed prior-spec surfaces (004 produces, 006 `autocond_<name>`/`asset_schedule`, 008 blocking checks, 012 `settings.yaml`/Settings page) enumerated as explicit dependencies with the behavior this feature relies on? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK036 - Is the assumption that partition kinds are limited to `none`/`daily` validated, and its effect on FR-007's one-to-one mapping made explicit? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 - Is the external-asset `depends_on` target boundary (conceptually valid, sensors out of scope) stated clearly enough to avoid ambiguity about what is testable this release? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions/§Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme (FR-###, SC-###) applied consistently across the spec so every item is individually traceable? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied; leave unchecked when the requirement still needs clarification or correction.
- `[Gap]` items flag requirements that appear absent from the current spec/plan — resolving them may mean adding a requirement or explicitly recording the omission as out of scope.
- `[Conflict]`/`[Consistency]` items flag statements that must be reconciled across spec.md, plan.md, and data-model.md (notably CHK014 on cycle-rejection semantics and CHK015 on manual-upstream `chain_depth`).
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify these markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; this file is a distinct custom checklist.
